summary: Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai, he taught Sanskrit and law before serving as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949) and practicing as a Senior Advocate.

Pankaj Jain studied at Karnatak University and the University of Iowa. A scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, he taught at North Carolina State University and the University of North Texas before becoming Professor at FLAME University in 2020.

Pankaj Tandon, a historian and Indologist, studied under mentor Tom Mallon-McCorgray and earned degrees from St. Stephen's College, Delhi School of Economics, and Harvard University (Ph.D. 1979). He served as an Associate Professor at Boston University from 1978.

Paolo Daffinà (d. 2009) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and Chinese history. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Giuseppe Tucci, Luciano Petech, and Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, later serving at Sapienza as Professor and Director (1973–1988).

Paolo Emilio Pavolini (1864–1942) was an Italian Indologist and linguist who studied under Emilio Teza, Albrecht Weber, and Richard Pischel at Pisa and Berlin. He spent most of his career at the University of Florence (1895–1935).

Paolo Visigalli is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Rome, University of Padua, and University of Cambridge, he has held posts at NYU Shanghai and Shanghai Normal University.

Paramahansa Yogananda (1893–1952) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He was educated in India, studying at Scottish Church College, the Senate of Serampore College, and the University of Calcutta between 1910 and 1915.

Paramita Paul is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and archaeology. She earned her Ph.D. from Leiden University in 2009 and has held positions as Chief Editor at the International Institute for Asian Studies and Lecturer at Amsterdam University College.

Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya (1891–1978) studied Indology and Buddhist studies under Louis de La Vallée Poussin and Sylvain Lévi. He served as Director of the Mithila Institute (~1954–1958) and General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI (1961–1972).

Paride Stortini is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Ca' Foscari, Padua, Antonianum, and Chicago (PhD 2022), he held posts at Chicago, Lake Forest, Tokyo (2022–2023), and Ghent University (2023).

Parimal G. Patil, a specialist in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, completed his studies at Harvard University and the University of Chicago. Around 2005, he was appointed Professor at Harvard University.

Parul Dave-Mukherji specializes in Indology, philosophy, and art history. She earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University from 2006 to 2026.

Pascale Haag is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat at Sorbonne Nouvelle and Marie-Claire Gay at Paris Nanterre. She has held posts at EHESS (from 2003), University of Hyderabad, and CY Cergy Paris University (2019–2023).

Pascale Hugon is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She has held academic positions at the University of Lausanne (attested 2006–2008), the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and its Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Pataraporn Sirikanchana works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a Professor at Thammasat University, attested in 2012.

Pathompong Bodhiprasiddhinand is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his DPhil from the University of Oxford (1998–2003) and served as an Assistant Professor at Mahidol University, attested between 2006 and 2011.

Patrice Ladwig is a researcher in Buddhist and religious studies. He has held appointments at the University of Bristol, the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012), and the Max Planck Society as Senior Research Fellow in 2016.

Patricia Berger is a specialist in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman. She was Curator at the Asian Art Museum and Professor Emerita at UC Berkeley.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey, a historian and Sinologist, earned degrees from Chicago and Columbia. She taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in the 1980s, visited the Institute for Advanced Study in 1998, and was Professor at the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia C. Stanley (1933–2003) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. After earning degrees from Chicago and UT Austin (Ph.D. ~1972), she taught at UT Austin, UT El Paso, Washington State University, and the University of Łódź (1976–1978).
